newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae director contests reorganization.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae director contests reorganization.

text.p: Albert Lord, a director of Student Loan Marketing Association, said Friday he and other directors voted against the company's previously-announced plan to reorganize into a private corporation.

Earlier, the association, better known as Sallie Mae, said its board had approved a plan to restructure as a fully private, federally-chartered corporation. Sallie Mae is the nation's largest source of college-education financing.
Lord said he agreed that Sallie Mae should be privatized but disagreed with the plan.

Lord said: "Sallie Mae did not disclose that I and seven other directors, constituting a majority of the shareholder-elected directors, voted against the proposed reorganization plan, including the board's decision not to name six of the existing shareholder-elected directors to the proposed new board."
Sallie Mae was not immediately available to comment.
It had said its reorganization plan included an 18-member board of directors, comprised of 10 members who have either served or are serving as directors and eight new nominees.

Sallie Mae's privatization was approved by Congress and signed into law by President Bill Clinton on September 30. The company said the plan would be submitted to shareholder vote at a special meeting on May 15.

"Congress and the administration have offered Sallie Mae the opportunity to structure a reorganization plan that can serve shareholders' interests and position the company for continued growth," Lord said in a statement. "The majority of the elected directors at Sallie Mae believe that the plan that was presented fell short of that goal."
